phenomena.description: No phenomenon: Belshazzar functions only as a chronological anchor for dating the vision; no act, speech, or disposition of his own is recorded.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "in the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar" -- no verb of his own

phenomena.description: Daniel's reception of a second, self-linked vision -- noted by his own hand as a sequel to a prior vision.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after that which appeared to me at the first" (H7200G, H0310A)

phenomena.description: Hostility escalates from territorial growth to a direct assault on the host of heaven and the stars -- casting down and trampling them.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "It grew great, even to the host of heaven. And some of the host and some of the stars it threw down to the ground and trampled on them"

phenomena.description: Self-magnification climaxes in an explicit comparison to a non-human figure ('the Prince of the host'), and turns concretely against the sanctuary system.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "It became great, even as great as the Prince of the host. And the regular burnt offering was taken away from him, and the place of his sanctuary was overthrown"

phenomena.description: Granted dominion (source outside itself, on account of transgression, left unnamed) turned to active hostility against truth, with success.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "it will throw truth to the ground, and it will act and prosper"

phenomena.description: A state of overhearing a dialogue between two non-human beings, not addressed to him.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "Then I heard a holy one speaking... another holy one said to the one who spoke, 'For how long is the vision...'"

phenomena.description: Reception of a specific, numbered answer to the question just overheard.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "And he said to me, 'For 2,300 evenings and mornings...'"

phenomena.description: An active disposition of seeking: Daniel's own will directed toward comprehension.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I sought [H1245] to understand [H0995] it"

phenomena.description: Continued auditory reception, now of a command given about him rather than to him.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I heard a man's voice... it called"

phenomena.description: A strong, embodied fear-response upon a non-human being's approach -- frightened, falling on his face.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I was frightened [H1204] and fell on my face"

phenomena.description: A state of total physical collapse under the encounter -- falling into deep sleep, face to the ground.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I fell into a deep sleep [H7290] with my face to the ground"

phenomena.description: A state of being addressed as the recipient of disclosure -- passive/receptive, content not yet given.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "Behold, I will make known to you what shall be..."

phenomena.description: Daniel's continued visionary perception now includes spatial self-location within the vision itself (Susa, the Ulai canal).
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I was in Susa the citadel... I was at the Ulai canal" (H1961 x2)

phenomena.description: Continued status as addressee, reminded of his own prior seeing as the basis for the interpretation now beginning.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "As for the ram that you saw" (2nd person)

phenomena.hib_label: the kings of Media and Persia
phenomena.description: The state of receiving its own resolved human identity -- named explicitly, closing the referential gap opened at v3.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "these are the kings of Media and Persia" (H4428)

phenomena.description: The state of receiving its own resolved human identity.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "the great horn between his eyes is the first king"

phenomena.description: The state of receiving its own resolved human identity.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "And the goat is the king of Greece"

phenomena.description: The state of receiving a qualified resolved identity -- genuinely arising from the first king's own nation, but explicitly denied his power.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "four kingdoms shall arise from his nation, but not with his power"

phenomena.description: Its fullest character-description yet -- bold-faced, skilled at understanding riddles -- inner faculties, not just acts, named directly for the first time, and its own resolved human identity given.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "a king of bold face [H5794+H6440], one who understands [H0995] riddles [H2420], shall arise"

phenomena.description: A disposition of destructive success explicitly sourced OUTSIDE its own power (left unnamed -- an insufficiency).
phenomena.textual_warrant: "His power shall be great -- but not by his own power; and he shall cause fearful destruction and shall succeed in what he does"

phenomena.hib_label: the people who are the saints
phenomena.description: A state of being the deliberate object of destruction, alongside mighty men.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "destroy mighty men and the people who are the saints" (H6944)

phenomena.description: The chapter's clearest, most explicit named interior state of any human figure: deceit prospering by his own cunning, self-exaltation located explicitly "in his own mind."
phenomena.textual_warrant: "By his cunning [H7922] he shall make deceit [H4820] prosper under his hand, and in his own mind [H3824] he shall become great [H1431]"

phenomena.description: The state of being given a closing instruction directly -- commanded to seal the vision.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "seal up the vision, for it refers to many days from now"

phenomena.description: The chapter's most extensive account of Daniel's own interior collapse: overcome, sick for days, then rising to resume ordinary duty, yet remaining appalled and explicitly failing to understand, even after the interpretation just given.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I, Daniel, was overcome and lay sick for some days... I was appalled by the vision and did not understand [H0995, negated] it"

phenomena.description: An act of deliberate visual attention -- Daniel raises his own eyes to look.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "I raised my eyes and saw, and behold" (H5375M)

phenomena.hib_label: the kings of Media and Persia
phenomena.description: A state of asymmetric strength between the two, depicted symbolically as a ram's two horns -- one higher than the other, the higher one having grown up last (Persia overtaking Media, per Gabriel's own later resolution, Dan 8:20).
phenomena.textual_warrant: "both horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last" (H1364 x3) -- resolved by name at Dan 8:20

phenomena.description: No new interior of Daniel's own beyond continued observation.
phenomena.textual_warrant: (no first-person interior content)

phenomena.hib_label: the kings of Media and Persia
phenomena.description: A disposition of unchecked self-will and dominance, depicted as the ram doing as it pleased and becoming great, with nothing able to withstand or rescue from it.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "He did as he pleased [H7522] and became great [H1431]" -- ram-imagery for the kingdom's own dominance

phenomena.description: Daniel's own interior state named directly for the first time: considering/discerning.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "As I was considering" (H0995)

phenomena.description: A state of conspicuousness/notability, singled out at the goat's very first appearance, depicted as its conspicuous horn.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "the goat had a conspicuous [H2380] horn between his eyes" -- resolved by name at Dan 8:21

phenomena.description: A mode of arrival marked by extraordinary swiftness and dominance of the whole visible earth, depicted as a goat crossing without touching the ground.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "across the face of the whole earth, without touching the ground" (H5060, negated) -- resolved by name at Dan 8:21

phenomena.description: No new interior of Daniel's own beyond continued observation of the confrontation.
phenomena.textual_warrant: (no first-person interior content)

phenomena.description: A disposition of powerful wrath directing its charge, depicted as the goat running at the ram.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "he ran at him in his powerful wrath"

phenomena.hib_label: the kings of Media and Persia
phenomena.description: No new disposition of their own -- carried over from v3, restated only as the object of the king of Greece's approach.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "which I had seen standing on the bank of the canal" -- no new verb of its own

phenomena.description: No new interior of Daniel's own beyond witnessing the violence.
phenomena.textual_warrant: (no first-person interior content)

phenomena.description: Wrath (v6) acted out physically in full -- enraged, striking, breaking, casting down, trampling.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "he was enraged against him and struck the ram and broke his two horns... trampled"

phenomena.hib_label: the kings of Media and Persia
phenomena.description: A state of total, helpless defeat -- broken, unable to stand, cast down, trampled, none able to rescue.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "the ram had no power to stand before him... he cast him down to the ground and trampled on him"

phenomena.description: The state of being broken precisely at the point of greatest strength -- sudden termination, not decline; his own kingdom's line ends here.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "the great horn was broken"

phenomena.description: A state of emergence/multiplication arising directly from the first king's own end, oriented toward the four winds -- dispersal of one kingdom's power among four successors.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "there came up four conspicuous horns toward the four winds of heaven" -- resolved by name at Dan 8:22

phenomena.description: A disposition of excessive, self-outgrowing greatness, immediately followed at its own height by the collapse of that same strength.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "the goat became exceedingly great, but when he was strong, the great horn was broken" (H1431, H7665)

phenomena.description: A disposition of small origin (arising from one of the four kingdoms) paired immediately with a drive toward extraordinary, multi-directional growth.
phenomena.textual_warrant: "Out of one of them came a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the glorious land" -- resolved by name at Dan 8:23
